alignments.note: The fronted prepositional phrase is the clause's predicate and takes the construction-supplied copula under rule 49, headed on the preposition; discontinuous under rule 25. The clause writes no subject but `מוֹקֵשׁ רָע` itself and the ASV writes no separate English subject for it, so the nominal is the subject and the `בְּ` phrase the predicate, exactly as in the parallel `בְּאֹרַח־צְדָקָה חַיִּים` of PRO.12.28. The competing reading gives *is* to `מוֹקֵשׁ` under rule 20.
Rectum with the chain's *of* and a supplied determiner (rules 19 and 15).
Predicate-following subject noun with its indefinite article (rule 15); the copula stands on the prepositional predicate under rule 49.

The ASV construes the adjective substantivally as a bare nominal and writes *to* for what it contributes (rule 33), with the supplied generic *man* of rule 31; headed on the lexeme. The margin *Or, an evil snare* was read and set aside under rule 38.
Finite verb with auxiliary; *out* is the phrasal particle completing `יָצָא`'s lexeme (rule 44).

review_notes: Copula moved from `מוֹקֵשׁ` to the `בְּ` heading the clause's prepositional predicate, bringing this verse into line with PRO.12.4, 12.19, 12.20 and 12.28, all of which read a fronted or postposed prepositional predicate under rule 49.
The printed text construes `רָע` as a separate nominal *to the evil man*; the margin's attributive reading was set aside under rule 38.
All 10 source and 21 target IDs partitioned exactly once.
